key_insight: UNSM changed hardness in Cr3C2–NiCr coatings in a strongly sample-dependent way, with detonation-sprayed coatings remaining more tightly clustered in hardness than HVOF coatings.
engineering_relevance: The results suggest UNSM can tune near-surface mechanical properties of thermal-spray coatings, but performance must be judged alongside local damage and surface integrity, not hardness alone.
method: Detonation-sprayed and HVOF Cr3C2–NiCr coatings were post-treated by UNSM.
Two static loads were used: 20 N and 30 N, with vibration amplitudes of 20 μm and 30 μm.
Hardness was measured by instrumented indentation at 300 mN/10 s, and post-scratch SEM morphology was examined.
evidence_signal: Measured hardness ranged from 820–970 HV for DS coatings and 546–1165 HV for HVOF coatings, with crack-like and heterogeneous SEM features observed after scratching.
watch_item: The abstract does not isolate whether observed morphology changes are caused by UNSM or by scratch testing, so scratch resistance ranking should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: HARDNESS AND POST-SCRATCH SURFACE MORPHOLOGY OF Cr₃C₂–NiCr COATINGS AFTER ULTRASONIC NANOCRYSTAL SURFACE MODIFICATION
